subject: Neptune MAP: performance execution plan + quant/kernel regressions
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@neptune.bio>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@neptune.bio>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Performance MAP and quant benchmarks for evaluation

Rohan —

Thanks for the call today. We want a short mutual action plan (MAP) that ties the performance benchmarks to procurement/close milestones so we can justify the pilot and budget. High level asks from our side:
- Clear TTFT, latency (P50/P95/P99), and sustained throughput numbers at target concurrencies (1, 8, 32).
- Quantization profiles (FP16/BF16 baseline vs INT8 and experimental INT4), with kernel-level timings and any observed regressions in output quality.
- A simple pass/fail acceptance criteria for the pilot so procurement can sign off.

We can share a 200-prompt evaluation set and a small trace of production throughput (non-sensitive). Can you sketch a timeline? Procurement prefers a close by mid-December if numbers land as expected.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Director of ML Engineering
Neptune Bio

Attachment: evaluation_prompts_sample.csv (csv)
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@neptune.bio>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Performance MAP and quant benchmarks for evaluation

Samir —

Thanks — this is exactly the right level of detail. I've attached a draft MAP (neptune_map_v1.xlsx) that maps evaluation milestones to procurement/close steps. Key points / proposed acceptance criteria:

MAP highlights (summary):
- Baseline model: Llama-3-13B / 8k context (we'll also sanity-check 32k traces). Baseline execution = FP16/BF16.
- Metrics to capture: TTFT (time-to-first-token), latency P50/P95/P99, sustained throughput (tokens/sec) at concurrencies [1, 8, 32], memory (KV cache), and kernel-level timings per layer.
- Quant profiles to run: FP16 (baseline), BF16 (optional), INT8 (per-channel symmetric), INT8-PTQ/per-tensor, and experimental INT4 (calibrated).
- Acceptance: functional quality regression <= 1.5% BERTScore delta OR <= 0.3 log-prob average delta on your eval set; performance improvement thresholds: INT8 >= 1.8x tokens/s vs FP16 at same hardware; TTFT P95 <= 350ms for single-request gen (target).
- Canary plan: 3-day canary at 10% traffic post-implementation with an automatic rollback if quality regression > 2.5% on sampled prompts.

Timeline (proposed):
- 11/24–11/30: MAP signoff + data handoff (you send 200 prompts + traces).
- 12/1–12/7: Performance runs + kernel profiling across contexts (4k/8k/32k) and quant modes.
- 12/8–12/10: Regression analysis, canary plan, and draft SOW/Procurement artifact.
- Target close: 12/15 (procurement to sign DocuSign)

Deliverables we will provide: benchmark CSV with per-request TTFT and per-token timings, kernel profile CSV (per-layer), an artifacts zip with sample traces (ttft-sample-traces.zip), and a short slide deck summarizing recommended config for production (batching, KV cache settings, quant profile).

I've included Marcus, Mina, and Sergio for technical and security/compliance signoffs. Marcus will own the kernel/profiling runs; Mina will validate the security checklist and artifact handling. Sergio will drive the SOW and can handle the DocuSign flow.

Are you okay with the acceptance thresholds above? If so we'll lock the MAP and start the runs on 12/1.

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments: neptune_map_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@neptune.bio>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T08:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Performance MAP and quant benchmarks for evaluation

Rohan / Samir —

Quick technical notes from runtime/kernel side so expectations are clear:
- Kernel profiling targets: per-layer forward attention kernel, MLP kernels, softmax, and KV cache read/write. We'll surface wall-clock + CUDA kernel durations in the CSV. Expect per-layer noise ~±5ms for small batches.
- Baseline perf expectations (approx): FP16 P95 ~120–180ms for single-turn 512-token gen on our V100/RTX-class test nodes; INT8 measured speedups typically 1.8–2.4x in tokens/sec depending on whether we can use fused attention kernels. INT4 is experimental — you'll likely see 2.8–3.6x speedup but with higher quality risk; we should gate INT4 behind additional QC.
- Memory/KV: INT8 reduces active model memory by ~2x vs FP16; INT4 can reduce further — watch KV cache fragmentation for long contexts.
- Regression checks: we'll run automated soft-checks (log-prob delta, token-level edit distance on canonical prompts) and a human spot-check on 20 prompts if thresholds are near the cutoff.

Action items for Samir: please confirm which hardware family we should target for the official numbers (A100-40GB, A100-80GB, or H200). Also send the 200-prompt eval and indicate the desired max output length for each prompt (e.g., 256 tokens).

I'll prepare the kernel instrumentation on our side and share a small run-book for you to reproduce locally if needed.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Systems Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachment: quant-kernel-instr-notes.md (text)
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@neptune.bio>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@neptune.bio>, Neptune Procurement <procurement@neptune.bio>
Date: 2026-11-24T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Performance MAP and quant benchmarks for evaluation

Thanks Rohan / Marcus —

A few clarifications from our technical and procurement side:
- Hardware target: please provide numbers on A100-80GB and H200 if possible. Procurement wants to know delta in price-per-token between the two.
- Context lengths: we'll need tests at 4k (most of our production), 8k (edge), and a 32k stress test for archival summarization.
- Output length: default max tokens 512 for the eval runs.
- Dataset: attached is the 200-prompt set and a short production trace with anonymized token counts.

Procurement note: final approval requires the MAP + a short performance summary that calls out risks and fallback plans. If you can deliver that by 12/10 we can push the legal review and close in the week of 12/13.

Regards,
Lena Ortiz
Senior ML Platform Engineer
Neptune Bio

Attachment: neptune_200_prompts_v1.csv (csv)
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@neptune.bio>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@neptune.bio>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T09:40:00-08:00
Subject: Updated MAP and schedule (final draft)

Samir / Lena —

Attached is the updated MAP (neptune_map_v1.xlsx) and an initial kernel-profile CSV (quant-kernel-results.csv) from a smoke run on A100-80GB. Highlights from the smoke run (short summary):
- FP16 baseline (8k context, 512 max tokens): TTFT P95 = 320ms; P50 = 140ms; sustained throughput = 85 tokens/sec at concurrency=1.
- INT8 (per-channel) on same hardware: TTFT P95 = 190ms; sustained throughput = 170 tokens/sec at concurrency=1 (2.0x tokens/sec vs FP16).
- INT4 (calibrated): TTFT P95 = 150ms; throughput = 230 tokens/sec (2.7x) but observed a small quality delta: avg log-prob delta ~0.25 and 1.8% BERTScore drop on the smoke prompts.

Per our acceptance criteria, INT8 passes (performance + quality), INT4 requires a post-canary human QC before production enablement. Attached CSV includes per-layer timing and top kernel names (fused_attn_fwd, mlp_dense_fwd, kv_store).

Next steps:
- 11/25–11/30: full batch runs across A100-80GB and H200 for 4k/8k/32k contexts (Marcus will run).
- 12/1–12/4: regression analysis and a short slide summary for procurement.
- 12/8: final MAP slide deck + SOW for internal legal.
- Target close: 12/15 (DocuSign link sent after procurement review).

Sergio — please prepare the DocuSign SOW placeholder and Mina — I'll ping you separately to confirm artifact handling for the traces/CSV (we'll keep sample traces locked and transfer via secure share).

Thanks — will update with the full CSV once Marcus completes the runs.

Best,
Rohan

Attachments: quant-kernel-results.csv, neptune_map_v1.xlsx, ttft-sample-traces.zip
From: Samir Patel <samir@neptune.bio>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@neptune.bio>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Updated MAP and schedule (final draft)

Rohan —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the smoke-run numbers. A couple of items from our side:
- Procurement is comfortable with the proposed acceptance thresholds. We'll sign if the full runs confirm the INT8 numbers and the INT4 human-QC path is documented.
- Security: we'll send our standard questionnaire to Mina — we need to confirm retention rules for traces and whether logs will ever contain PII (they won't in our uploads).
- Timeline: can we move the close target up to 12/13 if the A100/H200 full runs complete early? Procurement has a board review 12/14 and would like to include Redwood in that packet.

One small ask: please include an explicit regression-check step after the canary (automated + 20-manual prompts) and a note about restoring FP16 automatically if any regression metric exceeds the rollback threshold.

If that's in the MAP we can confirm and you can send the DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Samir
